title: Dressing
description: What the *map* looks like where the sim has only a tile class. A Low tile is 'cover you can shoot over' to every mechanism that walks, sees or shoots -- the sim knows nothing finer -- and this entry is what says the ones no parked vehicle covers are heaps of junk. Same rule as prop.schema.json and for the same reason (CLAUDE.md, 'how a thing looks is content, not code'): presentation/dressing.gd resolves keys out of this block and main.gd blits them, and neither contains a sprite key of its own. NOTE: the content validator is shallow -- it checks these top-level types and rejects unexpected top-level keys, and never once looks inside `wrecks` -- so the whole nested shape below is enforced by check_wrecks.gd, which resolves every key it declares and refuses a fabricated one.

id.description: Stable namespaced id. presentation/dressing.gd names exactly one, BLOCK_ID.

name.description: Human-readable name. Never shown to the player -- the district describes itself in prose, not in labels.

heaps.description: How a Low tile draws when no parked vehicle covers it: a heap of junk, one key per tile, picked by a pure hash of the map seed and the tile (never a sim RNG stream -- presentation may not spend a draw the layout would have to account for). Each key is an authored `prop` (assets/sprites/authored.json), never more than a tile across or tall, that presentation/main.gd hangs with its last row on the tile's south edge (Appearance.hang_rect) -- the outpost pack's rubbish bags, oil barrel and pallet stack since 2026-09-26, not a picture stretched over the tile. A Low tile a `map.vehicles` record does cover draws nothing here at all: the car is one feet-anchored three-quarter picture standing in the entity sort, and presentation/main.gd's tile branch defers the whole footprint to it. The two cases are mutually exclusive by construction and check_wrecks.gd holds the draw loop to it. The front/mid/rear car segment sets this replaced retired with the per-tile vehicle convention (docs/30, the Dungeon Settlers look, decision 11). An empty list draws the renderer's procedural cover block, which is the supported fallback.

litter.description: Cosmetic scatter keys for street pavement, hash-picked per tile and sparse. Purely decorative: litter marks nothing, blocks nothing and is drawn on tiles the sim considers empty paving.

rubble.description: Scatter keys drawn over tiles whose surface layer is SURFACE_RUBBLE -- the ground the worldgen rubble pass places. Unlike litter this one lies over something the sim does read (rubble slows a body and loudens a step), but the art still says nothing the surface did not already say.

walls.description: Wall material name -> {cap, face} sprite keys, one entry per building.schema.json / map.schema.json `look.wall` value. Optional, and the shallow validator never looks inside it -- it checks only that `walls` itself is an object -- so check_roof_look.gd is what resolves every key a shipped template's `look.wall` names and refuses one with no entry here.

roofs.description: Roof material name -> sprite keys, one entry per building.schema.json / map.schema.json `look.roof` value: `{n, s}` for a pitched material (north/south faces) or `{flat}` for a flat one. Optional, and the shallow validator never looks inside it -- it checks only that `roofs` itself is an object -- so check_roof_look.gd is what resolves every key a shipped template's `look.roof` names and refuses one with no entry here.

faces.description: Fixed sprite keys for the wall openings a building shell cuts, independent of wall material: `{window, door, garage}`. Optional, and the shallow validator never looks inside it -- it checks only that `faces` itself is an object -- so check_roof_look.gd is what resolves every key it declares and refuses a fabricated one.

trees.description: How a Tree tile draws: `tall` is a list of sprite keys, each an authored `tree` (assets/sprites/authored.json) -- the outpost pack's pine, broadleaf and dead tree since 2026-09-26 -- cropped to the pack's anchor row, that presentation/main.gd stands on the trunk tile's south-edge centre and y-sorts with the bodies, picked per tile by a pure hash of the seed and the tile (Dressing.SALT_TREE). A canopy may be wider than the trunk's tile (docs/30, 'The outpost pack, adopted'): the tree fades, never the body. Optional: a block with no trees draws the two procedural discs the tile branch always drew. The shallow validator never looks inside; check_trees.gd resolves every key at its authored canvas and refuses a fabricated one.

nature.description: Pictures lying on open outdoor floor that the sim still sees as open floor: bushes, reeds, rocks, stumps and logs. DRESSING, NEVER SIM STATE -- a picture here blocks no step, sightline or shot, is not cover, is not loot and is not a path anyone avoids, and nothing under godot/sim/ reads this list (check_trees.gd's INERT lane holds that). Each entry is one roll per tile: `key` (an authored `prop`), `surfaces` (SimSurface names, lower-case, the ground it may lie on), `rarity` (one tile in this many, at least two) and, for reeds, `beside: "water"` (a neighbouring tile stands on the water surface). Picked by a pure hash of the seed, the tile and the entry's index (Dressing.SALT_NATURE); the first entry that lands and fits wins the tile. A tile carries one only when it and its east and west neighbours are open outdoor floor. Optional: a block with no `nature` draws none. The shallow validator never looks inside; check_trees.gd's NATURE lane resolves every key and refuses a fabricated one.
